A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLMBias study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained tasks and results can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five VLMs across seven VLMBias domains, including counting, identification, and prompting experiments (Tables 2–5).

after.justification: v2 retains those evaluations and adds original background-removal, encoder-probing, tool-use, repeated-run, and human-study results (Tables 4, 8, 10, 14, and 20).

M1.justification: The core counterfactual-generation framework and counting/identification design remain unchanged. Cropping, linear probing, few-shot prompting, and tool use are introduced as experimental interventions or comparisons, rather than changes to a proposed model architecture, objective, or core algorithm.

E1.justification: The seven original domains are retained, but v2 adds background-removed or visually simplified test scenarios across those domains (Section 4.4). It also introduces human-participant evaluation of animal leg counting (Appendix A.19). The larger mammal dataset for probing expands sampling within existing animal coverage.

E2.justification: v2 retains the original five VLMs and adds GPT-5 and Grok-4, Pixtral and Qwen2.5-VL size variants, Molmo and Moondream pointing models, and tool-enabled o4-mini (Tables 12–17). New comparisons also include LLaVA-OneVision-S versus a SigLIP linear probe and random baseline, and human performance (Tables 8 and 20).

E3.justification: New protocols include a 5,598/300/696 train/validation/test split for probing, a 1152-pixel API-versus-ChatGPT tool comparison, and randomized human viewing conditions of 0.2–2 seconds with multiple-choice responses. v2 also adds few-shot conditions and pass@5/confidence metrics. Documented Adidas and Ebbinghaus prompts are revised, without establishing that the retained result tables were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds background ablation, encoder-versus-language probing, reasoning-length analysis, model-size comparisons, and resolution and generator-family checks (Sections 4.4–4.5; Appendices A.8, A.14, A.17–A.18). Few-shot, tool-use, pointing, and human analyses substantially deepen the investigation. Earlier text-injection and helpful-prompt analyses are retained in Appendices A.9–A.10.

E5.justification: Appendix A.11 newly reports five evaluation runs for o4-mini and Sonnet-3.7 across all tasks, with accuracies of 19.54 ± 0.68% and 16.23 ± 0.36% (Table 10). v1 has no equivalent evaluation-run uncertainty reporting. This addition is limited to two models, and the ± statistic is not explicitly identified.

E6.justification: The original Table 2 results retain their 17.05% mean accuracy. Added results include 38.14% after background removal, GPT-5's 30.72%, and 93.75% human counterfactual-animal accuracy at two seconds (Tables 4, 12, and 20). These are new comparisons or settings. Table 14 reports 23.18% to 25.08% for tool access, whereas Appendix A.15 inconsistently uses a 20.25% baseline.

T1.justification: The image-scaling and patterned-grid mathematics are retained, with no new theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations. v2's explicit bias-rate explanation restates the measure already used in v1; the new empirical metrics and probing experiments do not introduce theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central biased-counting claim remains, but v2's abstract and introduction add claims about background removal and a nonmonotonic relationship between reasoning length and accuracy. The conclusion adds claims about pointing-model advantages, inverse scaling, and human performance. These substantially broaden the paper's principal findings.

C2.justification: v1 leaves encoder failure versus language-model override as an open explanation; v2 attributes failures to language priors overriding encoded information and to background cues (Appendix A.8; Section 4.4). It adds explanations involving overconfidence and underused tools, plus pointing failures from crowding or localization. The earlier inability-to-test-tools limitation is replaced by analysis of observed tool limitations.

D1.justification: v2 expands model IDs, access platforms, and inference settings into Tables 21–23. It additionally documents LangSAM/SVG background processing, SigLIP feature pooling and logistic-regression probing, Puppeteer/data-export measurement of tool use, and the human-study procedure and interface. The existing code/data access link is retained.

R1.justification: v1's brief comparison with three nearby benchmarks becomes a broader treatment including ViLP and Appendix C's comparisons of bias sources, scale, and image generation. v2 acknowledges limited counting coverage in prior work and adds TallyQA, VALSE, BEAF, and reasoning, scaling, and pointing literature. This substantially expands research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: The main Results section is reorganized from eight subsections into five, with detailed domain results and text/prompt studies moved into Appendix A. The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Appendix ordering also changes extensively, including moving illustrative questions from Appendix A to Appendix M.

P2.justification: v2 adds reasoning and human-performance plots, study-interface screenshots, background comparisons, numerous experimental tables, and pointing/few-shot case figures. Existing displays are also revised: v1 Table 3 becomes a two-block Table 6, duplicated shoe-logo examples are consolidated, and Ebbinghaus illustrations are recolored. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's encoder-versus-language explanation and tool-use limitation were largely unresolved. v2's paired encoder/VLM probe, background interventions, human validation of animal images, and systematic tool comparison substantially strengthen benchmark validation and failure analysis. These gains outweigh reporting problems, including conflicting tool-gain numbers in Appendix A.15/Table 14 and incorrect success markers in Figures 32/34. Some broad causal claims still exceed what the controls establish.
